children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba — Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange could be heading downward going into October, said Jerry Klassen, analyst with Resilient Capital in Winnipeg.
Klassen cited a number of factors, ranging from harvest pressure increasing to China importing Australian canola.

Klassen said the main canola-growing areas on the Canadian Prairies, such as central parts of Saskatchewan and Alberta, will soon see the harvest accelerate. That in turn, he said will lead to more producer deliveries, which have been rather quiet so far this harvest season.
"We're going to see good harvest progress over the next seven to 10 days," Klassen said, pointing to a favorable weather outlook.
As the soybean harvest is getting fully underway in the United States, Chicago soyoil is also lower, the analyst noted, which has been weighing on canola values and shrinking its crush margins.
Klassen said the Statistics Canada production report on Sept. 16 greatly helped to bring clarity on the size of the 2026-27 canola crop.
StatCan pegged it at 22.05 million tonnes, down from last year's record harvest but still among the largest to be combined.
"We're maybe taking some of the risk premium out of the market," Klassen said of the canola estimate.
He added that "canola exporters are pretty well covered for their nearby commitments," which will reduce immediate demand.
"There's news that China bought Australian canola for the first time since 2020," Klassen said.
A report from UkrAgroConsult said the purchase was for 68,000 tonnes of canola.
Klassen warned that could have an impact on Canadian canola exports to China, the world's largest importer of the oilseed.
"It's maybe a trend that gets more significant for the Canadian canola crop," he said.

While Canada is the world's biggest exporter of canola, Australia is second. Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada projected 2026-27 canola exports of eight million tonnes, 1.1 million tonnes less than in the previous year.
Lachstock Consulting projected Australian canola exports to hit a record high 6.55 million tonnes, with 2.2 million expected to go to China.
